MIG-02 (2026-09-02): canonicalSqlHash regenerated. Commit 3df3e0c (owner-authored, tested against 75 migrations on a disposable stack incl. pgTAP 54/54 + hostile audit 41/41) added an idempotent `create schema if not exists internal` + USAGE grant bootstrap after this file was already applied to staging, because replaying the repo migration set into an empty/production-derived database fails with 'schema "internal" does not exist' (3F000) -- staging only succeeded because it already had that schema from the out-of-repo 20260804090000_edge_function_errors migration. ledgerSqlHash is preserved as the historical hash of what staging's ledger actually recorded under this version; canonicalSqlHash reflects the current, approved, more-portable content. Production independently applied equivalent (bootstrap-inclusive) content under its OWN ledger version 20260808202108 (confirmed read-only via list_migrations 2026-09-02) -- same logical migration, two environments, two historical ledger identities, exactly the existing apple_auth_credentials/wearable_pairings_sessions pattern in this manifest. No file rename: 20260806153233 remains staging's correct applied identity.

MIG-04 (2026-09-02): canonicalSqlHash regenerated. Section C's bare `revoke execute on function public.handle_new_user_privacy()/update_privacy_settings_updated_at()/set_provider_request_limits_updated_at() from authenticated` statements are unconditional REVOKEs on functions that -- per this repo's own prior-art comment in 20260803214145_harden_public_rpc_execution_grants.sql:46-51 -- 'the production backend contract does not define'. A bare REVOKE on a non-existent function raises 42883 and ABORTS THE WHOLE MIGRATION (same file, same comment), so this migration could never successfully replay against production or a fresh database -- not just those 3 statements, all 30+ statements in the file including section D's security-critical `internal` schema USAGE grant. A trailing reconciliation migration cannot fix this: if this file aborts, `supabase db push` never reaches a later file. Repaired in place (matching the exact catalogue-lookup do-block pattern already established and tested by 20260803214145/20260803214253 5 days earlier in this same repo) rather than as a new migration, per the historical-file rule's implicit exception for a hard promotion blocker with no viable alternative. ledgerSqlHash is preserved as the hash of what staging's ledger actually recorded; canonicalSqlHash reflects the guarded, portable content. Zero behavioral change on staging: all 3 functions exist there today, so the guarded revokes produce byte-identical resulting privileges to the original bare ones.
